disposition_reason: Table 1 prints mean +/- SD of nine metals (mg/kg dry) in maize flour milled with wooden and metallic mortars and eight diesel or electric hammer mills in Mbarara city.

study.design: Processing comparison survey of milled maize flour
study.origin: maize grain (origin not stated) milled in Mbarara city, Uganda
study.market: commercial hammer mills in Kamukuzi, Kakoba, Nyamitanga and Makenke divisions of Mbarara city
study.method: Oven drying at 85 C, HClO4/HNO3 hot-plate digestion, flame AAS (Perkin Elmer Analyst 100)
study.qa: procedural blanks; spike recoveries 98-100%; RSD 3.5-5.0%; no CRM

findings.notes: Maize grain milled in Mbarara city, Uganda, sampled December 2022 to March 2023; pooled by cone and quarter, oven-dried at 85 C (dry basis), HClO4/HNO3 digestion, flame AAS (Perkin Elmer Analyst 100). Spike recoveries 98-100%; RSD 3.5-5.0%. Mean +/- SD of 10 analyses (table note); n here is the number of flour samples for that mortar or mill as described in Methods. No LOD reported; many elements cluster near 0.50-0.60 mg/kg in every group (the text calls wooden-mortar Cd, Cr, Co and Ni 'traces'), which may reflect a reporting floor.

controls.outcome: Fe 19.23-19.39 vs 15.80-16.73 mg/kg; Pb 0.53-0.58 vs 0.53-0.55; differences stated as not significant

unresolved: No detection limits; the uniform 0.5-0.6 mg/kg values for Pb, Cd, Cr, Co and Ni across all mills, including the wooden-mortar control described as 'traces', suggest values near a quantification floor rather than true concentrations.
Table note says means are of 10 analyses, while Methods describe 12 flour samples per mill and 2 per mortar; n per group is uncertain.
The printed wavelength list does not match its element order (for example 324.7 nm, the copper line, is assigned to cadmium); not resolvable.
